summary: Targeted retest of Telegram Control auto-refresh bug fix + authorize flow. Backend: 3/3 pytest tests pass (GET /api/admin/telegram returns token_configured=true, bot.username=theairouterbot, webhook.url set; simulated webhook POST with correct secret creates pending user 700100200 with name=QA/username=qatester; POST /api/admin/telegram/authorize {"id":"700100200"} returns ok=true and moves id into settings.telegram_admin_ids while removing it from pending_users; webhook POST with WRONG X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token is a no-op and does not create a pending user). Frontend Playwright verified end-to-end: login with admin token → Settings tab → telegram-settings-card renders; clicking authorize-user-700100200 shows toast 'Authorized 700100200' and row detaches on next 4s poll; after resetting admin_ids via API the row auto-reappears purely from the 4s setInterval poll (no page reload) — bug fix VERIFIED; simulated webhook POST from within page.request.post returned 200; telegram-refresh-button present and clickable; dirty-ref guard confirmed — typed '999888777' into telegram-admin-ids-input, waited 5s across a poll cycle, value preserved (input NOT clobbered); telegram-test-button and telegram-webhook-button both present. No console errors.
action_items: State reset: settings.telegram_admin_ids was cleaned back to [] by the test at completion. However telegram_seen still contains id 700100200 (QA/qatester) plus a pre-existing real user 5682620043 (@sykopathic). If the main agent wants a fully empty pending list, purge those from the telegram_seen collection in MongoDB.
critical_code_review_comments: TelegramCard.js correctly uses setInterval(4000ms) with cleanup, and useRef dirty-flag prevents the poll from clobbering the ids input while the user is typing — matches the described fix.

GET /api/admin/telegram computes pending_users as (telegram_seen - admin_ids); authorize adds to admin_ids but does not delete from telegram_seen, so removing an id from admin_ids will re-surface it as pending. This is fine but worth noting for cleanup semantics.
Webhook route correctly rejects wrong X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token (verified: no pending user created).

rca of the issue: Original bug: TelegramCard only fetched status on mount, so users messaging the bot after page load never surfaced. Fix: useEffect now runs load() on mount plus setInterval(load, 4000) with cleanup; a useRef dirty flag prevents polled data from overwriting the admin-IDs input mid-typing. Verified live: authorize row auto-appears within one poll cycle of admin_ids changing without any page reload; typed input value survives poll cycles.
